newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTORCYCLING-"ALIEN" DOOHAN WINS FRENCH GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-"ALIEN" DOOHAN WINS FRENCH GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Australian Michael Doohan again outshone the rest of the pack with his fifth victory in six races this season at the French Grand Prix on Sunday.
"He's an alien. To finish second behind him is like victory for me," said Spaniard Carlos Checa, who was second ahead of fellow Honda rider Tadayuki Okada of Japan.
Doohan, the reigning world champion and current championship leader, covered the 31 laps in 42 minutes 38.064 seconds.
The Australian, who also won at Le Castellet last year, also clocked a fastest lap of 1:21.674 on his Honda, leaving his rivals wondering what to do to stop him.
Despite looking almost certain to take his fourth world title after winning in Malaysia, Japan, Italy, Austria and here, Doohan said his desire to keep winning was as strong as ever.
"I still want to win as hard as ever. I'm never tired of it," said Doohan, after clinching his 39th career victory.
"There is still a long season ahead of us," Doohan added.
His rivals have a difficult job of catching him in the championship standings, with the Australian now 43 points clear of his nearest rival, team mate Alex Criville of Spain.
Criville, who won the Spanish Grand Prix in May, was a disappointing fourth on Sunday.
Japanese rider Tetsuya Harada won the 250cc race ahead of world champion Max Biaggi of Italy.
